market_holds: Spot is about $3.2-3.3 (sealed 3.295 at 18:09 UTC; Yahoo hourly showed 3.215 at 14:31 ET), at a 52-week low and 67% below the high. The stock is down 21.5% over 5 sessions and about 18% in the last two (3.95 on Nov 17 to about 3.22). That drop came with peer Pony AI's Q3 print on Nov 18 (PONY opened +9%, was about -3.5% at 13:00 and closed -7.3%, then fell another 6% on Nov 19) and with a risk-off tape (QQQ reversed from 671 to 651 on Nov 19, KWEB at lows). WeRide has put out no news of its own since Oct 27. There is no usable option chain (ATM legs not two-sided) and no earnings history in the baseline. My own reading of the daily bars puts the last four print days at +14.7% (Nov 2025), a Mar 2026 date that is unclear, -0.8% close / -6.7% open (May 13, 2026) and -9.6% (Aug 12, 2026, Q2). Realised vol is 77% annualised, so the one-day deadband is 4.9%. Consensus is thin and unreliable: Chartmill shows revenue of about 270m (probably RMB, about +58% YoY against Q3'25's RMB171.0m) and EPS of -0.97 (probably RMB), while Earnings Whispers says no usable consensus exists. No numeric guidance was given at Q2. The long-range targets stand: 2,600 robotaxis by YE2026, positive quarterly cash flow from Q1 2028, breakeven in 2029, and a 100k ADAS unit year-end goal against about 30k shipped in Q2. Sentiment is bearish (Earnings Whispers bearish readings 59%, up from 15%; MarketBeat says short interest is up 17%). Cash was RMB5.4bn ($799m) at Jun 30, so the business is not distressed.
view: The stock goes into the print having lost about a fifth in a week, but almost none of that is tied to WeRide's own news. It came with Pony AI's print and with a risk-off Nasdaq and China-tech tape. Pony's quarter was operationally strong: revenue +75% to $44.6m, robotaxi revenue +165%, fleet 2,768. It still opened +9%, faded to about -3.5% by 13:00 ET and closed -7%. So the market's line for Chinese robotaxi names right now is not revenue growth. It is losses, R&D burn and the absence of a near-term path to profit. WeRide's Q2 showed the same split: revenue doubled QoQ and gross margin hit a record 37.5%, yet the stock fell 9.6% on the day because the loss did not narrow and R&D rose 36%. For Q3, WeRide is likely to show strong YoY revenue (the comp is RMB171m), and maybe a step up in ADAS units after the AION i60 launch on Sep 15, but probably a similar net loss (Q2 was RMB401m). That mix just got punished at Pony. Against that, WRD has already fallen more since Pony's print than Pony itself did, so a Pony-like disappointment is arguably in the price, and a clean ADAS ramp or narrowing loss could bring a relief move from an oversold base. Two risks cut the other way. Q2 was lumpy (+103% QoQ), so a sequential revenue decline is possible against a consensus that seems to assume growth. And the sector has a habit of fading pre-market strength through the morning, which counts here because the window closes at 13:00 ET. I cannot see the deciding line (the loss trajectory and ADAS volume), and I have no dated datapoint from inside the quarter that points either way. I lean slightly down on the sector's revealed reaction function and the tape, not on evidence about this company.

recommendation.reason: There is no dated evidence about WeRide's own quarter that the price misses. The 18% two-day fall came with a peer's print and the tape, and both point in opposite directions for this release: an oversold sympathy move against a market that sold Pony's strong-growth print. The deciding lines (net loss, R&D, ADAS volume, sequential revenue) are not visible before the release, and the consensus is too thin to say where the bar sits.
recommendation.what_would_flip_it: A clearly narrowing net loss or opex cut, together with a big ADAS unit step-up toward the 100k goal and sequential revenue growth, would make a relief bounce from this washed-out level the likely outcome through 13:00 ET.

self_critique: The strongest case against a slight down lean: WRD has fallen 18% in two sessions on someone else's news into a release with low expectations and rising short interest. Its cash ($799m) is close to its market cap, so a merely in-line print with a visible ADAS ramp could produce a sharp relief rally, which is what happened in Nov 2025 (+14.7%). A sympathy drop of this size with no own news is the kind of overshoot a release can reverse. The case for being more bearish: a lumpy sequential revenue decline after Q2's +103% QoQ, against a consensus that implies growth, would add fresh bad news to a falling tape. These cancel, which is why I stay near 50.
approach_notes: P6's run-in decomposition was the most useful part: it showed the drop was peer and tape, not company news. P4 kept me from treating the drawdown as a reason to call a bounce. The thin baseline (no options, no history) meant rebuilding past reactions from bars, which was cheap and worth doing.
